paragraphs: Rami bar Abba. Hullin 111, end of a: Rav Ashi visited the house of Rami bar Abba, his father-in-law. He saw Rami bar Abba's son skewering liver above meat and said, ‘How presumptuous is this rabbi!’ Yuhasin, under Aleph in its Rav Ashi entry, reports a version in which Rav Ashi married Rami bar Hama’s daughter (see that entry, where Heilprin leaves the question open). Yuhasin’s main text rejects that version and proposes Rav Assi, a contemporary of Rami bar Abba. Heilprin gives this as Rav Assi marrying Rami bar Abba’s daughter. The printed Yuhasin’s Shmuel gloss separately allows that the first match is possible. But it is difficult to emend to Rav Assi, for Rif and Asheri read Rav Ashi visited his father-in-law Rami bar Abba's house. Moreover, Rami bar Abba was in Rav Yosef's and Rav Huna's time; Rav Assi was Rav's pupil-colleague, much earlier. How could he marry his daughter? He questioned Rav Hisda's statement, came before Rav Pappa, who prohibited it, etc., then before Rav Huna, who prohibited it: Megillah 26b. It needs examination whether Rav Pappa and Rav Huna were in one generation: Rav Hisda was Rav Huna's pupil, Rava was Rav Hisda's pupil, and Rav Pappa was Rava's pupil. Eruvin 61a: Rav Yosef said that Rami bar Ammi said that Rav Huna said. This appears to be a scribal error for bar Abba, as I also found in the Berlin Talmud printing: Rami bar Abba. Rava was Rav Yosef's pupil. Perhaps Rav Huna here is Rav Huna bar Rav Yehoshua, Rav Pappa's colleague. He transmitted in Rav Huna’s name (Eruvin 10a). He transmitted in Rav Assi’s name (Eruvin 100b). Heilprin reports a Rav Ashi reading in Rif and Asheri. The checked Rif names Rav Ashi in the second teaching, citing Mari bar Abba, while the checked Rosh has Rav Assi in both teachings. R' Yosi instituted in Sepphoris: Sanhedrin 19, end of a. R' Yehoshua ben Levi said: Tanhuma, Bo. Ta’anit 17b quotes a teaching of his and then Rav Nahman’s report of Rabbah bar Avuha’s qualification. He transmitted two statements in Rav Yitzhak’s name (Berakhot 59b).
